rows: Numerous trees and fences blown down.

A section of fence was blown down with the posts broken off at the ground.

A theater sign and several large tree limbs were blown down.
Reported near the Hood/Johnson county line.

A 94 MPH wind gust was measured near Lake Granbury.
A life-size model of a stegasaurus was rolled several yards at Dinosaur Trails Cabins and Cottages. Damage to a large metal awning was also reported on Highway 377 East near Granbury.
A 67 MPH wind gust was measured in town.

Quarter size hail was reported 3 miles north-northwest of Granbury.

Quarter sized hail fell at the intersection of Farm-to-Market Road 51 and Farm-to-Market Road 167 north of Granbury.
Half dollar sized hail fell about 5 miles west of Cresson on Farm-to-Market Road 171.

A NWS Storm Survey determined an EF-0 tornado began approximately 2 miles southeast of Bluff Dale in Erath County and continued to the east into Hood County. This tornado had a path length of approximately 2.5 miles and an estimated width of 150 yards. Mostly tree damage occurred…

A NWS Storm Survey determined an EF-0 tornado began approximately 4.5 miles southwest of Tolar. This tornado had a path length of approximately 0.5 miles and an estimated width of 25 yards. Mostly tree damage occurred with this tornado and winds were estimated at 75-80 mph.
Quarter size hail fell near the community of Pecan Plantation.
Winds were estimated to be 60 MPH northeast of Granbury.
Sixty mph winds were estimated in Lipan. Power poles were knocked down.
Dime sized hail was reported in Lipan.
Golf ball sized hail was reported 2 miles east of Lipan.

Thunderstorm winds of 60 mph were estimated in the Sunset Acres neighborhood. A metal shed was blown into a neighbor's yard. The emergency manager reported wind damage to outbuildings stretched southeast to near the intersection of Meadow Wood and Rickabaugh Road.
Several fences and trees were blown down in the Gemstone Estates, northeast of Granbury. A 25-foot bradford pear tree was sheared in half. Other homes in the area suffered minor roof and shed damage.
Quarter sized hail was reported in Cresson.
Tree limbs that were 6 in diameter were knocked down in Granbury by thunderstorm winds. The winds were estimated to be at least 60 mph.
Strong thunderstorm winds knocked down a steel roof and metal rack onto 3 vehicles, damaging the cars.
Trained spotters reported penny sized hail in Granbury.
Golfball sized hail was reported near the Granbury High School.
The hail grew to the size of baseballs. Also, winds in excess of 50 mph were reported near the Granbury High School.

National Weather Service survey crew determined a tornado caused EF-0 and EF-1 damage in the Pecan Plantation community. The tornado began in Hood County, before moving across the Brazos into Johnson County.
Skylights and roofs were damaged at Acton Middle School, northwest of downtown Acton. A tennis court fence, wind screen, and portable bleachers were damaged as well.
A trained spotter reported quarter sized hail near Cresson.
Amateur radio operators reported golf ball sized hail in Granbury.
Penny sized hail was reported east of Granbury.

A mobile home on Missouri Trail was damaged when debris from an abandoned house next to them was thrown into the mobile home. The residents of the mobile home were displaced due to the damage. The COOP Observer in the area estimated 70-80 mph wind gusts.
Amateur radio operators reported a brief tornado northeast of Oak Trail Shores, on the east side of Lake Granbury / Brazos River.
The COOP Observer located 5 miles north of Granbury estimated 70-80 mph wind gusts.

Several trees and large tree branches were snapped north of Granbury.

A brief tornado was captured by broadcast media to the east of the city of Tolar. This tornado began near a mobile home park, damaging three homes. The tornado then crossed U.S. Highway 377 over an open field before dissipating.

A brief tornado occurred on the east side of the Brazos River / Lake Granbury early in the morning of March 8th. The tornado was photographed by several citizens, but occurred in open land near a golf course.
A social media report showed damage to a brick home, where the window was blown out and the chimney toppled.
